claims.statement: An ExplorationInquiry is a bounded reasoning activity opening possibilities around one or more related questions, with a target, source boundary and permitted outcome; its identity is distinct from a session or retained artifact.
An InquiryQuestion is a concern whose meaning and revision history matter to exploration; it need not already block a decision, and retaining its wording does not make it a truth-valued Claim.

An ExplorationFrame is the beneficiary, desired end, situation, scope, temporal horizon, premises and constraints under which a question or expression is interpreted; partial frames retain unknowns and distinguish governing constraints from revisable interpretations and implementation facts.

An ExplorationLens is an explicitly used perspective that makes particular distinctions salient; it describes an activity without requiring a pass or proving that a materially different expression resulted.

A CandidateExpression is a source-addressable articulation worth considering, including a question, fragment, outcome sketch, mechanism proposal or combination; it may remain unclassified and need not have an enduring prospective identity.

A TransformationAccount is an attributed Claim with Provenance connecting identified inputs, an asserted conceptual change and resulting expressions; it preserves a consequential explanation without establishing an internal cognitive trace, deterministic derivation or causal creative improvement.

A PossibilityLandscape is a bounded, revision-scoped view of expressions and asserted relationships under an identified inquiry and frame; overlapping groupings and acknowledged omissions do not imply an inventory of all possible futures.

An ExploratoryJudgment is an attributed Claim about novelty, similarity, difference, grouping or an inquiry limit, preserving subjects, criterion, comparison basis, source and revision scope, assessor and material uncertainty; it supplies no ranking, selection or action authority.

The divergent exploration reference-case document contains source-pinned historical annotations and one explicitly illustrative incomplete expression, and labels them as representation work rather than fresh qualification trials.
